title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing pp. 393ff of the 'équation des lacets' notes). Π_{0,3}^ is the profinite completion of a group containing the profinite fundamental group π_{0,3}^ of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, extended by the S_3 symmetries. It is generated by π_{0,3}^ together with σ_∞ of order 2 (z ↦ 1−z, swapping 0 and 1) and ρ of order 3 (cyclic permutation of 0,1,∞). The overall structure is essentially the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. Π~ is a slightly larger variant. The loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ are the standard inertia generators. Lowercase σ_∞(x), ρ(x) denote conjugation by σ_∞, ρ.

The objects u ∈ M^{!~}_{0,3} are automorphisms of Π_{0,3}^. Each sends σ_∞ and ρ to conjugates of themselves, compatibly with the cusp structure. They form a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group.

On the previous page Grothendieck parametrized u by triples (α,β,f), with α_0 = f^{-1}α and β_0 = f^{-1}β. The parametrization is taken modulo the simultaneous left multiplication by l_0^n, n ∈ Ẑ. It is subject to the 'relation des lacets' (37): αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} · l_1^ν. He also set ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}.

On this page:
(42) u(σ_∞) = int(f^{-1}β)(σ_∞) and u(ρ) = int(f^{-1}α)(ρ). Hence (42bis) u = int(f^{-1})∘u_{α,β}, where u_{α,β} depends only on (α,β).
(42ter) u_{α,β}(σ_∞) = βσ_∞β^{-1} = (βσ_∞(β)^{-1})σ_∞ = ησ_∞. Likewise u_{α,β}(ρ) = αρα^{-1} = ξρ. The next page confirms u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(ησ_∞) and u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ).
(43) is (37) rewritten: ξ = η l_1^ν.

Section 4 passes to the parameters (ξ,η,f).
- Constraints (44): ξ ρ(ξ) ρ^2(ξ) = 1 and η σ_∞(η) = 1. These hold automatically for ξ, η of the form (41), because ρ^3 = 1 and σ_∞^2 = 1. They are equivalent to (ξρ)^3 = 1 and (ησ_∞)^2 = 1.
- Conversely, Grothendieck asserts that every solution of (44) arises from some α, β. This amounts to the claim that every torsion element of order 3 (resp. 2) in the profinite free product, lying over the class of ρ (resp. σ_∞), is conjugate to ρ (resp. σ_∞).
- Thus u corresponds to triples (ξ,η,f) modulo the l_0^n-action and subject to (44) and (46) = (43): ξ = η l_1^ν. He calls (46) the 'commutation relation between ξ and η'.

The next page notes the advantage: the equations are maximally simple, f is absent, and for ν = 0 the relation is just ξ = η. It also notes drawbacks: three equations instead of one, and the images of ξ, η in SL(2,Ẑ) carry little information.

Modern reading: with η = f(x,y) and ξ = f(x,y)·x^m (m = ν), the three relations are exactly Drinfeld's defining equations of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group:
- the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1;
- the 3-cycle (hexagon) relation f(x,y)x^m f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m = 1, with λ = 2m+1.
In this sense the page is a 'decoupled' presentation of GT^ in which the 2- and 3-cycle conditions are imposed on separate unknowns, linked by a single relation.
errors: Machine transcription: in (42) the second formula should read u(ρ) = int(f^{-1}α)(ρ), not f^{+1}α, consistent with α_0 = f^{-1}α from (38).
Machine transcription: in (42ter) u_{α,β}(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) equals ξρ, not ξρξ^{-1}. Indeed αρα^{-1} = αρ(α)^{-1}ρ; the next page confirms u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ).

Gap: the claimed equivalence 'data (α,β) ⇔ data (ξ,η) satisfying (44)' is asserted without argument. The direction from (44) back to (α,β) needs the conjugacy of finite-order elements in the profinite free product Ẑ/2 * Ẑ/3, i.e. a profinite Kurosh-type theorem (Herfort–Ribes type). It also needs care about which coset (Π vs Π~) the conjugator lies in, and about the residual indeterminacy of α, β by centralizers of ρ and σ_∞.

Minor sign/convention point: the induced action on ξ, η of α ↦ l_0^n α (and β ↦ l_0^n β) is ξ ↦ l_0^n ξ ρ(l_0)^{-n} and η ↦ l_0^n η σ_∞(l_0)^{-n}. Writing these as l_0^n ξ l_1^{±n} depends on the conventions for ρ(l_0) and σ_∞(l_0); the exponent sign in the manuscript cannot be checked from the image. In any case the relation ξ = η l_1^ν is compatible with the action, since powers of l_1 commute.

ideas.what: Parametrizing automorphisms u of the profinite Z/2*Z/3-type group (preserving the conjugacy classes of σ_∞, ρ) by conjugating elements: u(σ_∞) = int(f^{-1}β)σ_∞ and u(ρ) = int(f^{-1}α)ρ, with u = inner ∘ u_{α,β}
ideas.modern_name: Description of GT^ / outer automorphisms of profinite PSL(2,Z)-type groups via conjugators of torsion generators
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and the action on π_{0,3}, π_{1,1} but not these formulas; La Longue Marche (1981) manuscript, partly discussed by Lochak/Schneps

ideas.what: Decoupled equations (44): ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 (3-cycle) and ησ_∞(η) = 1 (2-cycle), linked by ξ = η l_1^ν
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's 2-cycle and hexagon (3-cycle) relations defining GT^, with ν = m = (λ−1)/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 ('On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras and a group closely connected with Gal(Q̄/Q)')

ideas.what: Rewriting the torsion conditions as (ξρ)^3 = 1 and (ησ_∞)^2 = 1, i.e. ξρ and ησ_∞ are torsion elements conjugate to ρ, σ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Conjugacy of finite subgroups in profinite free products

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes down an explicit presentation of his group M^{!~}_{0,3} by triples (ξ,η,f). The equations are a 2-cycle relation on η, a 3-cycle relation on ξ, and the link ξ = η l_1^ν. This is equivalent to Drinfeld's defining relations of GT^ with λ = 2ν+1, a decade before Drinfeld. Grothendieck's anticipation of GT is folklore, but this specific decoupled form with separate unknowns does not appear as such in the literature. In that form, ξ and η are distinct unknowns and the 'commutation relation' reduces to ξ = η when λ = 1.
missed.quote: la donnée de u ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~} équivaut à celle d'un triplet (ξ,η,f) ... satisfaisant les relations (44), et la relation (46)=(43) ξ = η l_1^ν, qui joue le rôle de "relation de commutation entre ξ,η"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents precisely how close the 1981 Longue Marche notes came to GT^. It also gives a slightly different formalism, with α, β as conjugators of the order-3 and order-2 generators. That formalism might be useful for studying GT^ via profinite PSL(2,Z) and SL(2,Ẑ) images, a direction he flags on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, essentially complete derivation of GT-type defining equations from the 'équation des lacets', predating Drinfeld. Specialists (Lochak, Schneps) know Grothendieck anticipated GT in the Longue Marche, so the existence of such equations is not a shock. The explicit decoupled (ξ,η,f) form is, however, a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: (42ter): the boxed formulas read u_{α,β}(σ_∞) = int(β)(σ_∞) [= ησ_∞] and u_{α,β}(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) = ξρ, not ξρξ^{-1}.
(42bis): 'u = int(f^{-1}) u_{α,β}' — the manuscript writes 'int' (next page 'inn').
Section 4: the domain of (α,β) is \tilde{Π}_{0,3}^ × Π_{0,3}^, as on the previous page.
Indeterminacy line under (45): the exponent sign of l_1 (l_1^n vs l_1^{-n}) is uncertain.
